title: Rewrite composite index strategy and null FK simplification for control plane
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Background: The control plane has accumulated several overlapping composite indexes across tenant, entity, and event tables. Many queries still hit sequential scans for multi-tenant reads because current composite indexes include nullable FK columns in inconsistent order. This ticket will rationalize composite index shapes, remove redundant nullable FK columns from hot-path indexes, and introduce replacement partial indexes and not-null FK canonicalization to reduce planner uncertainty and bloat. Goals: (1) reduce 95th and p99 read latency for tenant-scoped queries by 30-50% for common routes, (2) reduce index storage by ~15% on targeted tables, (3) make online migrations reversible with minimal downtime. Scope: events, control_events, tenant_metadata, and entity_lookup tables. Out of scope: billing ledger and audit_event large-append tables (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: New index set reduces median query time for /controlplane/tenant reads by >=25% in staging
p99 for the 5 tracked queries drops by >=30% in staging compared to baseline
Index on events table shrinks storage footprint by >=10% after reindex (measured in bytes/index) in staging
All migrations run online with a graceful fallback path; rollback completes within 30 minutes without schema incompatibility
Schema change migration is signed off by DB+SRE and code owners for control-plane queries
migration_plan: Create partial not-null shadow columns for nullable foreign keys (e.g., fk_tenant_id_nn) and backfill in small batches
Add new partial/composite indexes that reference shadow not-null columns and include frequently filtered cols (status, created_at) as leading keys
Gradually switch application query paths to prefer new indexes using query hints/optimizer statistics adjustments in staging
Run live A/B on staging: 50/50 traffic split for 48h, collect latency and EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans
Once stable, reindex using CONCURRENTLY in production during low-traffic window with monitoring and canary queries
Drop redundant old indexes with CONCURRENTLY after 72h stable metrics; keep drop commands in a safe runbook
rollback_plan: If p99 regressions or index corruption observed, immediately revert application query hints and route traffic to previous region/replica set if available. Restore dropped indexes from runbook snapshot -- we will not drop indexes in production until 72h of stable telemetry. If CONCURRENT reindex encounters failures, abort and open ENG-rollback-run; use pg_repack or standby promotion as measured fallback.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DB layer changes (ORM index hints) and CI that runs explain plans against a representative dataset
Staging performance soak: 48h A/B with synthetic traffic and sampled production query replay
Chaos run: kill and restart replicas during reindex to validate online robustness
Schema compatibility tests: ensure old clients can still write and read until final migration step
benchmarks: Baseline: staging run 2025-10-07 - median tenant read 42ms, p99 310ms for tracked queries
Storage baseline: events index size ~480GB; expected reduction >=45GB after compaction/reindex
